raw_response:
I’m 53 this year, and I’ve farmed these 8 mu for many years, so I mostly do what has worked steady for me. We do wheat and maize in turn, that’s the safe way here. With only 2 people in the household and some off-farm work, I can’t make things too complicated. I use the well when the crop really needs it, but water and electricity cost money, so I won’t irrigate too many times. For wheat, I’ll sow around the usual October time, use a common improved seed from the local dealer, put most fertilizer as base fertilizer, then add a bit more in spring if the field looks weak. Wheat cannot be starved, otherwise yield drops too much. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll hurry to plant maize right away. The turnaround is short, so I won’t do heavy tillage, just simple field prep and sow quickly. For maize I still use fertilizer, but not too much, because cash is tight and last year medium input was already acceptable. I watch what neighbors do, and most people around here manage about like this. I want steady grain, not taking big risks.
